findings.text: ci_gate.py cmd_status maps every GhError to verdict 'none' exit 0 and has no cannot_run verdict or exit 2 path in status (cannot_run exists only in parity for missing bash). test_status_gh_unavailable_is_none_exit_0 asserts the opposite for a generic GhError, so the AC's missing-gh=none vs unusable-gh=cannot_run split is untested and unimplemented.

findings.ac: Status: a gh failure after the first read is pending
findings.text: gate_status calls _gh inside the poll loop with no try/except; a GhError on a later poll propagates to cmd_status and becomes verdict 'none' (exit 0, a skip) instead of 'pending'. No test makes the second gh pr view raise; FakeGh never fails.

findings.ac: Status: a failing log fetch keeps the PR red and big
findings.text: _failing_detail calls _gh('run','view',...,'--log-failed') unguarded; a GhError there aborts gate_status and cmd_status returns verdict 'none' exit 0 (a false pass on a red PR) rather than red + class big. FakeGh.logs always supplies the log, so no test exercises a failing log fetch.

findings.ac: Fix path: exit 2 halts `[CI-RED] could not check`
findings.text: The literal '[CI-RED] could not check' is absent from src/references/ci-gate.md and the 4a/3z/3d workflows (only '[CI-PARITY] could not run' exists), and test_ci_gate_wiring.py has no assertion for a status exit-2 halt.

findings.ac: Classifier: big for a parsed failure in an untouched file whatever the job is named
findings.text: classify() skips any failure whose check/step/log_tail matches MECHANICAL (lint, format, drift, black, ruff, eslint, install dependencies...) before looking at parsed test files, so a pytest failure in an untouched file in a job or step named 'lint' or 'Install dependencies' is classed small. test_classify_big's 'untouched' case uses check 'test'/step 'Run tests' only, so the 'whatever the job is named' direction is unproven.

No test asserts result['base_stale'] is True from gate_status or main; the gate fixture pins _base_is_stale to False and the stale case only calls classify() directly with a hand-passed flag, so the wiring of _base_is_stale(baseRefOid) into the output field and class is unverified.

findings.ac: Constitution and build: version: stamps are bumped
findings.text: 3d-implement-issue (2.6.0), 3z-afk-loop (1.7.0) and 4a-verify-and-ship (1.5.0) have identical version values at dea48fc, 7091e37 and the main fork point, though their bodies changed; only the constitution (3.4.0) and the new reference are asserted by test_ci_gate_wiring.py, so the AC's stamp bump is unmet and untested for the workflows.

findings.ac: Scope: parity subcommand vs issue body
findings.text: The issue Overview/Notes state pre-push parity was dropped (two subcommands: status and cap), but ci_gate.py still ships `parity`, 4a step 4 still runs it before push with [CI-PARITY] halts and parity:waived, the reference section 1 and the fix order include `parity`, and tests assert it. This adds ship-path time the issue rejected and diverges from the AC fix order (suite record, commit, cap, floor guard, push, re-check).

findings.ac: Time-to-Value: run with the host's maximum tool timeout
findings.text: The 480 s default and in-script deadline are tested, but no doc literal tells the caller to run the status call with the host's maximum tool timeout or describes the single blocking call (no 'timeout' text in references/ci-gate.md or the 4a step 7/8 wording), so a host default timeout would cut the wait.

findings.ac: Fix path: single round and re-check at --attempt 2
findings.text: _fix_order_ok only checks the token 'status --attempt' and 'At most 2 fix commits'; the reference says `--attempt <k>`, never the literal `--attempt 2`, and no test asserts the single re-check round ('re-run once') in 4a step 8 or that 4a's second status runs at attempt 2.
